conditional-types.summary: Conditional types are type-level if/else: `T extends U ? X : Y`. Combined with `infer`, distribution, template literals and recursion, they let you compute types from other types.
points: `extends` in a conditional type is an assignability check. `infer X` binds a type variable from the match and is usable only in the true branch.
A naked type parameter distributes over unions: each member is checked separately and the results are unioned. Wrap both sides in a tuple, `[T] extends [U]`, to turn this off.
`never` is the empty union, so a distributive conditional over never returns never. `any` returns the union of both branches.
Several `infer X` candidates in covariant positions combine into a union; in contravariant positions (function parameters) they combine into an intersection. That is how UnionToIntersection works.
Template literal types multiply unions and can parse strings with `infer`; `infer N extends number` converts numeric strings into number literals.
Recursive conditional types in tail position run up to about 1,000 iterations (TS 4.5+); recursion inside spreads or other types hits the depth error far sooner. Use accumulators.
Inferring from an overloaded function uses its last signature, and a conditional return type on a generic function stays deferred, so returns need overloads or assertions.
traps: `T extends never ? true : false` returns never for never; use `[T] extends [never]`.
`boolean` is `true | false`, so it splits in distributive conditionals and counts as a union.
Mapping over a function type (for example in a naive DeepReadonly) turns it into `{}` and drops its call signature.
